name: Ketovore

lead: Ketovore is very low-carb eating centred on meat and animal fat, with a small selection of plant foods allowed. People follow it to drop body fat and the puffy, bloated look, with a plate that is easy to plan.

The chain is lower carbohydrate intake, which pushes the liver to make ketone bodies as an alternative fuel, and followers report reduced appetite and less water retention, so the face and midsection look leaner. The name is informal and no trials have tested ketovore itself; the research comes from ketogenic and low-carb diet studies.

paras: Most people build meals around beef, eggs, fish and animal fats, then add a few low-carb vegetables or other plants for variety and fibre. It is usually followed as an everyday eating style rather than a short cleanse, and followers commonly report early scale changes within the first weeks as water and appetite shift.

Ketogenic diets can cause constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and clinical use is medically supervised. Dietetic bodies describe the neighbouring carnivore diet as a fad diet and cite low fibre and higher LDL cholesterol. People with kidney, liver or lipid conditions, or who are pregnant, should check with a clinician first.

angle.text: Ketovore is used for keto-style fat loss with a simple meat-centred plate, aiming for a leaner body and less bloat. Cutting carbs lowers appetite and water retention, which shows up as a slimmer, less puffy look. Research comes from keto and low-carb diets generally, as the hybrid has no trials of its own.

lead: Ketovore is an informal label for a diet that combines ketogenic, very low-carbohydrate eating with a meat-heavy emphasis, while still allowing some plant foods. It sits between a standard ketogenic diet and the carnivore diet, which allows only animal products [1][2].

The ketogenic diet is a high-fat, adequate-protein, low-carbohydrate diet used in conventional medicine mainly for drug-resistant epilepsy [2]. The carnivore diet is classed by dietetic bodies such as the British Dietetic Association as a fad diet, and no clinical trials of it were cited on Wikipedia [1]. No clinical trials of a diet specifically called ketovore were found.
infobox: Meat-centred, very low carbohydrate, some plants

paras: The term is used informally rather than defined by a medical body. It generally denotes a keto diet in which animal foods dominate and a limited set of low-carbohydrate plants is included. A related variant, the animal-based diet, adds fruit, honey and raw dairy to carnivore eating [1].

Wikipedia reports that carnivore eating excludes fruit and vegetables, is low in fibre, and can raise LDL cholesterol, and that dietitians and physicians have called it potentially dangerous [1]. In clinical use of ketogenic diets, reported adverse effects include constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and the diet requires medical supervision to start [2].

A 2025 cross-sectional study described people who achieved type 2 diabetes remission through diet and exercise changes in real-world settings and examined their glucose-monitoring profiles in relation to dietary pattern [3]. It did not test a ketovore diet for appearance.
